about: User-facing names of the workflow's gates and task statuses. Internal ids (G1-G8, T1-Tn) stay in files, state, and logs; people see the titles. Edit titles and explanations here; do not change ids or document/key, which the helper reads.

gates.title: Requirement Clarification
gates.purpose: Settle the questions the PBI and its documents leave open before anything is specified.
gates.activities: Read the refined PBI and supporting documents, list missing inputs, contradictions, and unclear terms.
gates.deliverable: Answered or explicitly deferred questions, recorded in spec section 9.
gates.review: Answer each question or mark it as deferred.
gates.afterApproval: The answers become authoritative and the specification uses them.

gates.title: Existing Code Analysis & Gap Assessment
gates.purpose: Find what already exists before anything new is planned.
gates.activities: Map every requirement to source documents and to existing code as EXISTING, REUSABLE, EXTEND, NEW, or UNKNOWN, with file and line evidence.
gates.deliverable: The gap map in spec section 3a: counts per classification, every NEW and UNKNOWN row, conflicts between documents.
gates.review: Whether each requirement is classified correctly and whether existing code was missed.
gates.afterApproval: The technical specification is written from the approved map.

gates.title: Technical Specification Review
gates.purpose: Agree on what will be built before planning how.
gates.activities: Write scope, business rules, entities and states, contracts, acceptance criteria, assumptions, and open questions.
gates.deliverable: spec.md with a readiness verdict and numbered acceptance criteria.
gates.review: Business rules, acceptance criteria, contract changes, and the open questions.
gates.afterApproval: The implementation plan is written against the approved specification.

gates.title: Implementation Plan Approval
gates.purpose: Agree on the file-level changes before any source file is edited.
gates.activities: Break the work into named tasks, each with files (reuse, modify, new), evidence, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and checks; run the spec-plan consistency gate.
gates.deliverable: plan.md with descriptive task titles and the consistency findings.
gates.review: The task list, the files each task changes, and the validation approach.
gates.afterApproval: Implementation starts with the first task, test first; no source file is edited before this approval.

gates.title: Build, Test & Quality Verification
gates.purpose: Prove the change works and meets the quality bar.
gates.activities: Build, run focused then wider tests, coverage of changed lines, analyzers and Sonar sources, pre-PR review, scope check.
gates.deliverable: The verification report: requirement-to-test matrix, baseline versus final counts, Sonar table, open items.
gates.review: Anything reported as failed, not run, or not verified.
gates.afterApproval: The corporate security check runs, then the handover is final.

gates.title: Corporate Security Check
gates.purpose: Check, from evidence, that the work followed the security controls; it never stands for corporate approval.
gates.activities: Authorization, data handling, secrets and suppressions, dependency changes, Sonar, script safety, isolation, memory, installer integrity, Git operations.
gates.deliverable: corporate-security-report.html in the task's evidence folder with PASS, FAIL, NOT VERIFIED, or NOT APPLICABLE per control.
gates.review: Every FAIL and NOT VERIFIED control.
gates.afterApproval: The work is handed over; commit and push still need your separate instruction.
